name: sky-photo
title: Sky Photo
description: Reads a photo of the sky locally: its EXIF (orientation, capture time and offset, GPS, compass heading, focal length and 35 mm equivalent) with a small parser of its own, its sky found by a classical skyline finder (colour, brightness and texture, a skyline per column by dynamic programming, holes and masts, a feathered mask) with no model to download, the photo's own clouds and window panes to light at night, and a rectilinear projection from a sun azimuth and altitude to the photo and back, with calibration from one marked point.
docs: `analyzeSkyPhoto(src | blob, { skyMask?, signal? })` from `@/lib/sky-photo` resolves with `{ width, height, aspect, exif, mask, sky, foregroundUrl, analysisMs, dispose() }`: `sky` is a canvas opaque where it is sky, `foregroundUrl` an object URL of a PNG for `mask-image`, freed by `dispose`. The finder runs at 512 px on the long side in stages, yielding to the page between them (60 to 90 ms in all on a laptop); `findSky(pixels)` runs it in one go, for a worker or a test. A cross-origin URL needs CORS. `readSkyPhotoExif(bytes)` and `readSkyPhotoExifFrom(blob)` (`@/lib/sky-photo-exif`) never throw; `findSky` lives in `@/lib/sky-photo-mask`. From `@/lib/sky-photo-projection`, `projectSky(view, azimuth, altitude)` maps a sky direction to `{ x, y, behind }` from 0 to 1 over the photo for `view = { heading, fov, horizon, aspect }`, `unprojectSky` maps back, `calibrateSkyView({ fov, aspect }, sun, point)` finds the heading and horizon that put the sun on a marked point, and `fovFromFocalLength35mm(focal, aspect)` reads the field of view from EXIF. `findClouds(pixels, mask)` and `findWindows(pixels, mask, { share?, seed? })` (`@/lib/sky-photo-features`) give alpha maps of the photo's clouds (how covered, how lit) and of a seeded share of its window panes; `analyzeSkyPhoto` returns them as object URLs with `clouds: true` and `windows: true`. The finder works at 1024 px; thin crisp structures (a lattice tower, a crane) stay foreground and specks of cloud texture don't.
